report:
**Conclusion:** Your view is correct: there is no reliable evidence that soursop (also called graviola or *Annona muricata*) cures cancer in humans.

**Why the claim persists:** There is legitimate *preclinical* research. Extracts and compounds (annonaceous acetogenins) have killed cancer cells in laboratory experiments, and some animal studies suggest antitumor effects. For example, an NCI-linked publication reports effects on pancreatic-cancer cells and animal-model experiments. But cell cultures and animal models do not establish that a substance is effective, safe, absorbable at a useful dose, or superior to standard therapy in people.  
https://edrn.cancer.gov/data-and-resources/publications/22475682-2053-graviola-a-novel-promising-natural-derived-drug-that-inhibits-tumorigenicity-and-metastasis-of-pancreatic-cancer-cells-in-vitro-and-in-vivo-through-altering-cell-metabolism/

**What is missing:** Human cancer trials showing that soursop cures cancer—or improves survival, tumor response, or quality of life—are lacking. Memorial Sloan Kettering specifically notes anticancer findings across several *cell lines* but says human studies are lacking. Cancer Research UK likewise concludes there is not enough reliable evidence for graviola as a cancer treatment.  
https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/graviola  
https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/about-cancer/treatment/complementary-alternative-therapies/individual-therapies/graviola

**Safety:** “Natural” is not synonymous with safe, especially for concentrated leaf/seed teas or supplements. Published research links consumption of *A. muricata* fruit and leaf preparations to concern about atypical, levodopa-resistant parkinsonism, plausibly related to its acetogenins.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16078200/

Soursop fruit can be food, but it should not replace evidence-based cancer treatment. Anyone with cancer considering soursop extracts should discuss them with their oncology team, particularly because supplements can cause toxicity or interact with treatment.
